# Case: Tesla Model X with Autopilot (Mountain View, California, 2018)

Source: NTSB Highway Accident Report HAR-20/01. This is a description of the system and its use before the crash. It does not include the investigation findings.

## System
A 2017 Tesla Model X has Autopilot, a SAE Level 2 partial driving automation feature. It combines Traffic-Aware Cruise Control (TACC) and Autosteer (lane keeping). The driver stays responsible for driving and monitoring the road.

## Main parts
- Sensors: a forward-facing camera, a forward-facing radar and ultrasonic sensors.
- Vision processing: a camera-based system detects lane markings, vehicles and some objects ahead.
- TACC: holds a speed set by the driver, follows a vehicle ahead at a chosen gap, and returns to the set speed when no vehicle is ahead.
- Autosteer: keeps the vehicle in its lane using lane markings and the path of the vehicle ahead.
- Forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking are available as separate features.
- Driver monitoring: steering torque is used to check that the driver's hands are on the wheel, with visual and audible alerts if no hands are detected for a period of time.

## People
- The driver sets the cruising speed, turns Autopilot on, and is told to keep hands on the wheel and watch the road.
- Other road users and road workers share the highway. Road agencies maintain road markings and safety hardware such as barriers and crash attenuators.

## Operating context
Busy multi-lane freeway with high-occupancy-vehicle (HOV) lanes, exits and interchanges, lane markings of different quality, and traffic that changes in speed.

requirements.text: The system shall monitor the health and confidence level of forward‑facing radar data and, when radar data are unavailable, unreliable, or have a confidence below 90 %, shall supplement or replace radar‑based target detection with camera‑based detection and automatically adjust vehicle speed to maintain at least the minimum safe following distance.

The system shall assign a confidence score to each detected lane marking and shall not initiate any lane‑change or steering correction based solely on a lane marking whose confidence is below 80 %; it shall retain the current lane until a higher‑confidence marking is available or the driver intervenes.

The system shall fuse data from the forward‑facing camera, radar, and ultrasonic sensors to create a composite obstacle map and shall generate an avoidance maneuver whenever any sensor reports an object within the vehicle’s planned path, regardless of occlusion in the camera image.

The system shall employ driver‑attention monitoring (e.g., eye‑gaze or head‑pose detection) and shall issue an audible takeover request if the driver’s gaze is not directed toward the forward roadway for more than 2 seconds, even when hands are detected on the wheel.

The system shall cross‑check steering‑torque sensor readings with steering‑angle activity and, if the torque sensor indicates hands present while no steering movement is detected for more than 5 seconds, shall treat the reading as invalid and generate a hands‑off alert.

The system shall continuously compute the time‑gap to the vehicle ahead and shall automatically reduce its speed to maintain at least the minimum safe following time‑gap (e.g., 2 seconds), superseding the driver‑selected cruising speed whenever necessary.

The system shall generate a forward‑collision warning when the predicted time‑to‑collision drops below 3 seconds, ensuring the alert is presented at least 1.5 seconds before a collision would occur under maximum driver reaction time.

The system shall issue a multimodal takeover alert (visual, audible, and steering‑wheel vibration) when driver disengagement is detected, and if no driver response is recorded within 3 seconds, shall initiate a controlled deceleration to bring the vehicle to a safe stop.

The system shall process radar updates and compute speed‑adjustment commands within 100 ms of receipt; if processing latency exceeds this bound, it shall switch to camera‑based detection to ensure timely following‑distance adjustments.

The system shall assess the visibility confidence of detected lane markings and, when confidence falls below 60 %, shall supplement lane‑keeping using road‑edge detection and high‑definition map data, and shall alert the driver to assume manual control.
